items.reason: No Then step checks a production result or effect, so R1 yields no principal. Lane A's setter principal is a trivial setter (R4) that cannot influence the checked flag; update is never executed, so R1/R7 give no evidence for it; nothing is generated or third-party, so R6 zero-body does not fit. Amendment 3.2 ('Then steps check only test-side state') applies. Removing the representative removes this 8-requirement implementation group from all six cells.

Both lanes agree and the evidence confirms it: the checked exception is produced by test code, no production body decides it, and a requirement-named principal (update) would be hidden without any relation to what is checked (amendment 3.2).
Same as :213; in addition the checked exception type has no production realisation under this glue (amendment 3.2).

The Then step checks a test-side flag set by a glue NullPointerException. The only production contribution is the documented null-on-empty contract of a trivial accessor, which stays stated in its retained Javadoc, so hiding its body removes nothing; the requirement's own rule is never exercised. This is the closest of the four calls: if the owner prefers to keep it, use lane A's entry (R4 allows hiding an accessor whose default the scenario depends on).
